Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

be verb

also am, is, are, was, were, been, being, I am …ing (the continuous tenses), be + past participle (the passive)

classical

Ter. And. 194: Dāvus sum, nōn Oedipūs.
Aug. Conf. 9.11.27: ubi eram?
Traupman 277

sum, esse, fuī, futūrus

verb, irregular · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Its forms: sum, es, est, sumus, estis, sunt (am, is, are); eram (was, used to be); fuī (was, have been); erō (will be); infinitives esse, fuisse and fore (= futūrum esse). Short sayings often leave est out: omnia praeclāra, rāra (Cic. Amic. 79). “There is” has its own record (there is).

Other words

  • legō, legēbam — I am reading, I was reading

    the present and imperfect tenses: no auxiliary · also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 577–578: Tē ēcastor praestōlābar.

    Latin has no continuous tenses: “I am reading” is legō, “I was reading” legēbam. Quid agis? is both “what are you doing?” and “how are you?”.

  • vincor, victus sum — I am beaten, I have been (was) beaten

    the passive: one word in the present system; the perfect participle with sum in the perfect system · also used · classical · Liv. 22.7.8: pugnā … magnā victī sumus

    English “be” with a past participle is the Latin passive. In the present, imperfect and future it needs no auxiliary (vincimur, we are being beaten); in the perfect, pluperfect and future perfect it takes sum (victī sumus, victī erāmus).

Examples

  • ubi eram?

    Where was I?Aug. Conf. 9.11.27

  • quot estis?

    How many of you are there?Petr. 92.1

  • quī fuit rāna, nunc est rēx

    the one who was a frog is now a kingPetr. 77.1

  • nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē

    none of us is the same in the morning as he was the day beforeSen. Ep. 58.22

  • rārum genus! et quidem omnia praeclāra, rāra

    a rare kind! and indeed all fine things are rareCic. Amic. 79

  • quid agis, mea fēstīvitās? — Tē ēcastor praestōlābar.

    How are you, my darling? — I was waiting for you, I swear.Plaut. Cas. 577–578

  • pugnā … magnā victī sumus

    we have been beaten in a great battleLiv. 22.7.8
